name: Name
body: Battle Forge is a monthly series that presents a new WARMACHINE scenario in each installment. Battle Forge scenarios emphasize the narrative unfolding over the course of a game and may be asymmetrical, uneven, and even somewhat experimental because the goal of Battle Forge is to create a sandbox toolset that allows for creative scenario generation and new, story-worthy experiences with WARMACHINE! Players are encouraged to modify Battle Forge scenarios in any way that makes the scenario more appropriate for their army collections and their available terrain resources. Most important of all, have fun! And if you find a better way to do something with a scenario that results in a better experience for you, let us know at feedback@privateerpress.com, so we can try it, too!

name: Name
body: Following are the key terms that will be repeated in many Battle Forge scenarios:

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models, uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective, uncontested.

name: Name
body: Battle Forge victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set amount of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body: In addition to its standard rules, each Battle Forge scenario has two random tables that add additional Victory Point-scoring opportunities for players that vary each time the scenario is played. Mission Modifiers add additional scoring opportunities based on the position of a player’s models on the table. Achievements add additional scoring opportunities based on a player’s actions taken on the battlefield. Players should roll a d6 to randomly determine Mission Modifiers and Achievements before the beginning of a game, or players can choose them at will if all players agree. It is recommended that only one Mission Modifier and one Achievement should be in effect during any match (unless you really want to get crazy).

name: Name
body: If a player makes an attack that destroys one or more friendly models, that player’s opponent gains 1 Victory Point. If a player makes an attack and destroys their own Leader model, that player immediately loses the match.

name: Name
body: In addition to objectives, Battle Forge scenarios will routinely draw on the following terrain elements. Dimensions provided are approximations, and you should feel free to substitute any terrain pieces you have available as necessary. Use the resources you have available to get close enough to maintain the spirit and intention of the scenario.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 3/4" x 4". Barriers provide cover.

name: Name
body: Obstructions with an approximate footprint of 5" x 5".

name: Name
body: Forest areas with an approximate footprint of 5" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 2" x 2". Small obstacles provide cover.

name: Name
body: An elevated platform at least 1" above the table, such as a hill or terrace. Plateaus can possess multiple areas at different heights that models can be placed on, but the areas must be level to prevent models from falling over. If a model cannot be placed on a level area without risk of falling off, it cannot occupy that area. Models cannot be placed on slopes, and we recommend that plateau terrain with sloped surfaces not be used. Plateau, Small—A plateau platform with a footprint approximately 6" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 30 mm models to be placed on. Plateau, Large—A plateau with a footprint approximately 6" to 12" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 40 mm models to be placed on.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of rubble approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: A 3" x 5" trench template.

name: Name
body: Recon forces have discovered the enemy's command center hidden within a small village. Assault it and extract any valuable intel for examination by high command.

name: Name
body: "Enemy Intel" is designed for 50- and 75-point forces.

name: Name
body: "Enemy Intel" ends after seven rounds.

name: Name
body: Players take the role of either the Attacker or the Defender. The Attacker must penetrate the enemy’s command bunker, seize their intel, and escape with it. The Defender must protect their valuable intel at all costs.

name: Name
body:
Score Victory Points as the Attacker by breaching the opponent’s bunker, seizing the intel, and escaping with the intel to your deployment zone.
Score Victory Points as the Defender by repelling your opponent’s forces, protecting your command center, and preventing the intel from reaching the attacker’s deployment zone.

name: Name
body: This scenario uses the map layout below. Place one bunker, two small forests, four medium buildings, and four small barriers on the table as shown on the map. If you don’t have this exact assortment of terrain, use what you have to create a diverse environment with an emphasis on maintaining lots of line-of-sight blocking terrain to protect the Attacker’s forces as they approach the bunker.

name: Name
body: At the start of the game, before deployment, the Defender may elect to start the game with one small-based unit with no more than five models, one medium-based unit with no more than three models, or one small- or medium-based solo deployed within the bunker. All warrior models in the Attacker’s army gain the Extract Intel special action: Extract Intel (H Action) – RNG 1. Target a bunker with no enemy models occupying it. This model is now considered to be carrying the intel. All Cohort models in the Attacker’s army are equipped with heavy, expensive, and precise equipment specifically for this special operation and gain the Breaching Charge special action: Breaching Charge (H Action) – Target a bunker within 1". At the start of your next turn, the target bunker suffers 4d6 damage, and all models occupying the bunker are removed from play. If a model carrying the intel is destroyed or removed from play, the controlling player must place a 30 mm token anywhere in base contact with the model before removing it from the board. This token represents the dropped intel. Any model contacting the token during its Normal Movement can remove the token from the board and is now considered to be carrying the intel. If the bunker is destroyed before the intel is extracted, the intel is lost!

name: Name
body:
Intel may only be extracted from the bunker once per game.
The Attacker takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
Starting on the third round, when a player begins their turn, they gain 1 Victory Point if they are occupying the bunker or 2 Victory Points if they are occupying the bunker with two or more warrior models and no enemy models are within 2" of it. Additionally, Victory Points can be scored as follows:
The Attacker gains 1 Victory Point the first time they use the Breaching Charge special action against the bunker.
The Attacker gains 2 Victory Points if they extract the intel from the bunker.
A player gains 1 Victory Point the first time they enter their deployment zone with a model carrying the intel.
If the Defender destroys the bunker before the intel is extracted, the Attacker immediately wins. If the Attacker destroys the bunker before intel is extracted, the Defender gains 2 Victory Points.

name: Name
body: Roll once on both the Mission Modifiers and Achievement tables.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Mission Modifier for this match: 1. Held at Bay— Beginning with the third round, score 1 Victory Point at the beginning of your turn if your opponent’s Leader is within 12" of the rear edge of their deployment zone. 2. Secure the Perimeter— Beginning with the third round, score 1 Victory Point at the end of each of your turns in which your opponent has no models on your side of the table. 3. Debunking— The Attacker scores 1 Victory Point if they destroy the bunker. The Defender scores 1 Victory point at the start of each of their turns starting on the fourth round in which the bunker is not destroyed.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Achievement for this match. 1. Unleashed Power— Gain 1 Victory Point each time one of your models deals over 30 points of damage in a single turn. 2. Bloodletting— Gain 1 Victory Point the first time one of your models damages an enemy Leader with an attack each turn. 3. Skilled Garrison— Gain 1 Victory Point when your model occupying a bunker destroys or removes from play an enemy Cohort model.

name: Name
body: Victory conditions are checked in the following order: Decisive Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, if the Attacker has a model with the intel within the Attacker’s deployment zone, the Attacker wins the match. If at the end of the first player’s seventh turn the bunker is in play and the intel has not been extracted, the Defender wins the match. Point Advantage Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with 6 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match. Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match. Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match. At the end of six rounds, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match.

name: Name
body:
"Enemy Intel" is a flexible scenario that can be easily altered to provide all new experiences. Here are some things to try in any combination:
• For playing at the 100-point level, replace the bunker with two bunkers combined together without the back door pieces. One of the Defender’s small- or medium-based units can begin the game deployed inside of the bunker regardless of the unit size. The combined bunker is treated like a bunker with 70 health. Treat the seam where the bunkers are joined as the entry point, as if they were ladders used to reach the hatches.
• If you have a Guard Tower or two, swap out one or two of the buildings on the Defender’s side of the table with Guard Towers with the doors facing the Defender’s deployment zone. The Attacker scores 2 Victory Points for each Guard Tower they destroy.
• Make the assault upon the bunker a raid at dawn. Treat all models on both sides as having stealth for the first two turns of the game. The Defender may place two Fire Pit defenses at the start of the game.

name: Name
body: • For an increased challenge, require the Attacker’s Leader model to extract the intel.
